# Umbraco Rules

Project conventions, enforced by code in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco` where possible. The short version of the ten UmbraCommandments.

1. **Never put content behind a composition.** Removing a composition permanently deletes its content on every document that used it — no recovery through revisions. Compositions are for meta, settings, CTAs. Litmus test: *if we remove this composition later, is what remains still viable content?*
2. **There are six kinds of document type — file each in its folder.** Page (renders), Block (renders; lives in block list/grid; never used as a composition), Composition (composed onto others; never rendered, never pickable), Data (element; never renders — settings, events, people), Repository (container node; never renders), Repository Item (the pickable records inside a Repository).
3. **Data types never sit at the root of the data type tree.** Built-ins under `/Umbraco/<editor>`, custom ones under `/Custom/<editor>`. `DataTypeSavedHandler` enforces this on every save.
4. **Register in an `IComposer`, not Program.cs.** If `IUmbracoBuilder` can do it, it belongs in `Composers/`. Non-Umbraco concerns (CORS, App Insights) go in `WebApplicationBuilder` extension methods.
5. **Production runs in production mode.** Umbraco Application Url set, `--configuration Release`, HTTPS only, no model generation, no template editing. `appsettings.json` ships configured this way — don't soften it; put dev conveniences in `appsettings.Development.json`.
6. **Aliases are English and camelCase.** No exceptions.
7. **Dictionary keys are PascalCase with dots** (`My.Dictionary.Item`), and a dictionary folder never has values of its own.
8. **Media always lives in a folder.**
9. **The content root only holds Repositories.** The site hangs under the WWW `siteRoot` node; going multi-site means adding another Page beneath it, not re-architecting. Because WWW never renders, the site Page needs a **domain** or nothing answers on `/` — assign `/` for a single site, a hostname each for several.
10. **uSync everything — commit `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/uSync/`.** Export is automatic; you should not need to trigger it. On Umbraco Cloud, use Umbraco Deploy instead.

value.markup:
MCP — the Model Context Protocol — is an open standard that lets an AI model talk to tools the same way your browser talks to printers: through a protocol almost nobody needs to think about.

A server, a client, three verbs

Clients connect to servers. Servers expose three things:

  • Tools — functions the model can call, declared once, executed anywhere.
  • Resources — data the model can read before it starts answering.
  • Prompts — reusable instruction templates.

That is the whole spec. What makes it valuable is not the list — it is what the list implies: a model can now reach into your CMS, your database and your command line without anyone writing bespoke glue per app.

value.markup:
The easiest way to misread MCP is as yet another API pier: a point where your app meets someone else's. That framing hides the real geometry.

Nodes, not spokes

With MCP, your content management system, your media library, your build pipeline and your vector store all expose the same wire. The model is not a hub the world plugs into — it is one more node on a graph where anything can talk to anything.

  1. A server that can read turns files into resources.
  2. A server that can write turns actions into tools.
  3. A server that can do both becomes infrastructure.

Look at the image block above this post: the picture did not come from an upload form. It came from a folder on disk, read by a media server, picked by a document model, and placed into a block grid member — all over the same protocol that wrote this paragraph.

A server, a client, three verbs

Clients connect to servers. Servers expose three things:

That is the whole spec. What makes it valuable is not the list — it is what the list implies: a model can now reach into your CMS, your database and your command line without anyone writing bespoke glue per app.

Post 1's blocks look great — everything landed. The only issue: `ctaLink` external url is empty in the read-back. The external link value I sent had `url`, `name`, `query`, `target`, `linkType`. The read-back normalized it to include `type: "external"`, `queryString`, `unique`, but `url` is "".

This is suspicious. Maybe the create-document-block write path normalized the link model and the url field isn't mapped from `url` — or maybe external url actually got saved but the read-back's `url` is displayed differently... no, url is clearly "".

The read-back shape suggests the server's LinkModel: fields `icon, name, published, queryString, target, trashed, type, unique, url, culture`. My input used `linkType` and `url`. The server mapped `linkType`→`type` and `query`→`queryString` but `url` got dropped? Or maybe when the input uses key `url` with a value, the normalization... hmm.

Let me test: use update-document-block-property on the front page hero's ctaLink setting value with the proper read-model shape including `type: "external"` and `url: "https://..."` and see if it sticks. Actually, a more reliable approach: since these are external links in a demo, maybe replace with links that surely work. But the url being empty would render href="" which is broken.

Let me try updating one block's ctaLink with the canonical shape. I'll use update-block-property (the tool for updating block content) with value:
```
[{"name":"Read the posts","queryString":null,"target":"_self","trashed":false,"type":"external","unique":null,"url":"https://modelcontextprotocol.io","culture":null,"icon":"icon-link","published":true}]
```

Let me test on the front page hero block 5d172c1f (property ctaLink), then read back to confirm.

Actually — wait. Maybe the url was dropped because my input object for the external link included `"linkType": "external", "url": "https://..."` but the MCP tool's property-value path passes through and the management API's LinkPropertyValueEditor converts. The read-back shape has "type":"external". So my "linkType" became "type". And "url" → "url". It shows "" — meaning the url value didn't round-trip through my input? I definitely sent url. Unless... the value object's url key got consumed by the normalization that maps display urls, and for external links the management API expects the `url` on the link to be set but the stored value uses it... I'm not sure.

Let me look at a known-good external link value. In v14+/15 the raw value for MultiUrlPicker external link stored in DB:
```
[{"name":"...","queryString":"","target":"_blank","culture":null,"url":"https://...","type":"external"}]
```
So the raw value uses `url` (not displayUrl). My input matches roughly. The read-back normalizes to `{"icon":"icon-link","name":"...","published":true,"queryString":null,"target":"_blank","trashed":false,"type":"external","unique":null,"url":"","culture":null}`. url is empty though. Strange but maybe this read-back `url` field is a placeholder computed (for external it should be the same). 

Hmm, I wonder if the MCP server's create-document-block normalizes link values and strips url for "external" unless... Actually maybe it's the reverse: the normalization happens because my "url" key was there but the server created a LinkItem with Url property from a different key. Whatever the cause, the practical fix: update the ctaLink values with the read-back object shape INCLUDING url, and confirm it persists.

Let me try with update-block-property on front page hero block.

  2. A server that can write turns actions into tools.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: The user asked me to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server by building a simple blog site: (1) a front page listing blog posts, and (2) two blog posts about why MCP is awesome. Constraints from the task message (verbatim intent): - Build everything with blocks and the block grid. - Order of operations: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create Razor views (step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco because generated models land on disk but the running site holds the old assembly; must stop site, `dotnet build`, restart, THEN write views that compile against the models). - Umbraco was stopped by the user; I must start it with `dotnet run` in the Umbraco project before using the MCP server. - Always use the MCP server to create content; do not write any migration plans as part of this test. - For images, use only the Unsplash photos in the `unsplash/` folder (see its README), import into the media library; do not download other images. Media lives in a folder (rule 8). - Clean-room exercise: work only inside the project folder; don't look in parent/sibling folders or other projects (package caches like ~/.nuget are fine); don't read or write any memory. - Work autonomously; user won't answer questions. - When done, finish with a short report: what was built, how to view it, and anything not working. - Must adhere to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md exactly (block rendering via Umbraco's own conventions: `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`/`GetBlockListHtmlAsync`, adapter partials at `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/.cshtml` (camelCase alias, capital C in Components), one ViewComponent per block in `Views/Shared/Components//Default.cshtml`, `Service` naming in `Services/`, no loose `.cs` in `Models/`). 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Umbraco CMS v18.2.0 (.NET 10), SQLite dev database, uSync schema export, ModelsBuilder (SourceCodeAuto in development, models in `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Models/ModelsBuilder/`, namespace `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco.Models`) - Umbraco MCP server (`@umbraco-cms/mcp-dev@18`) connecting to https://localhost:44317 (client id `umbraco-back-office-mcp-local-only`, secret `mcp-local-dev-secret-b3ll4b00t-not-a-real-secret`) - Six document-type folders: Pages, Blocks, Compositions, Data, Repositories, Repository Items - Block Grid (v15+ value shape: layout/contentData/settingsData/expose arrays referencing contentKey/settingsKey) - MediaPicker3 value shape: `[{"key":"","mediaKey":"","crops":[],"focalPoint":null}]` - MultiUrlPicker external link value shape (canonical): `[{"name":...,"published":true,"queryString":null,"target":"_self","trashed":false,"type":"external","unique":null,"url":"https://...","culture":null,"icon":"icon-link"}]` - Tiptap richtext value: `{"markup":"

","blocks":{"layout":{},"contentData":[],"settingsData":[],"expose":[]}}` - Dropdown (Umbraco.DropDown.Flexible) items are a plain string array in v18 (NOT objects with id/value) - Block Grid `validationLimit` is enforced literally (max=0 means zero blocks allowed); must be null to mean "no limit" - blockSettings as a *composition* on block content element types (not a separate settingsElementTypeKey in the Block Grid config), so anchor/spacing are content-level block properties - ILSpy (`ilspycmd`) for decompiling Umbraco assemblies in ~/.nuget - Management API token: POST /umbraco/management/api/v1/security/back-office/token (no audience param), curl direct API access for validation details 3. <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <CompressionEnabled>false</CompressionEnabled> <!-- Disable compression. E.g. for umbraco backoffice files. These files should be precompressed by node and not let dotnet handle it -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Umbraco.Cms" />
    <PackageReference Include="uSync" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <!--
      Opt-in to app-local ICU to ensure consistent globalization APIs across different platforms.
      Default mirrors prior behaviour introduced in https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/pull/11276: enabled unless building on macOS without an explicit RuntimeIdentifier.
      To override:
        * Build/publish:  dotnet publish -p:UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu=false
        * Post-publish:   edit System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu in the published *.runtimeconfig.json
      Note: DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_APPLOCALICU is only honored when AppLocalIcu is absent from runtimeconfig.json
      (verified on .NET 10) — the general .NET 9 env-var-precedence rule does not apply to this knob, since it is
      resolved by the native host before the CLR boots. Use one of the two override paths above instead.
      Keep UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion in sync with the referenced Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime package version.
    -->
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == '' and ($(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('linux')) or $(RuntimeIdentifier.StartsWith('win')) or ('$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == '' and !$([MSBuild]::IsOSPlatform('osx'))))">true</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == ''">false</UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu>
    <UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion Condition="'$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)' == ''">72.1.0.3</UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(UmbracoUseAppLocalIcu)' == 'true'">
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime" />
    <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.AppLocalIcu" Value="$(UmbracoAppLocalIcuVersion)" />
  </ItemGroup>


  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Razor files are needed for the backoffice to work correctly -->

## What I built

A two-post blog site demonstrating the Umbraco MCP server end to end, built entirely with blocks and the block grid, following the prescribed order: **model → content → rebuild → Razor**.

**Content model (all via MCP, no migrations):**
- **Page types** — `blogFrontPage`, `blogPost` (with Title/Intro/Blocks and Summary/CoverImage/PublishedDate/Blocks), each with a template. The front page got the `/` domain.
- **5 block element types** — `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`, `callToActionBlock`.
- **1 composition** — `blockSettings` (anchor + "Block Spacing" dropdown) composed onto every block, so anchor/spacing are content-level block properties.
- **Data types** — a Block Spacing dropdown and a Block Grid; all filed under the scaffold's six folders.
- **Content** — front page (hero → richtext → CTA) and two published posts ("Why MCP Is Awesome: Plumbing…" and "MCP as a Network: Every Tool a Node", each hero → richtext → image → quote → CTA, with external CTA links to modelcontextprotocol.io). All 10 Unsplash photos imported into a `Blog` media folder and used via MediaPicker3.

**Razor (Umbraco's own rendering pipeline, no custom renderers):**
- Templates render blocks with `@await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")`; the front page lists published posts via `Model.Children<BlogPost>()` with signed `GetCropUrl()` crops.
- 5 adapter partials at `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` → 5 ViewComponents (`Hero`, `RichText`, `Image`, `Quote`, `CallToAction`), plain models in `Models/Blocks/`, markup in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` (Tailwind).
- Added the (missing) `umb-block-grid` layout CSS + rich-text typography to the Frontend Tailwind bundle and built it into `wwwroot/dist`.

- **Block Grid validation gotcha** — the Block Grid data type enforced its `validationLimit` literally (`max: 0` = zero blocks allowed) and every publish failed until I set the limits to `null`. Fixed via MCP before publishing.
- **Rich text double-encoding** — in v18 `IHtmlEncodedString` is *not* `IHtmlContent`, so `@Model.BodyText` emits escaped markup. Fixed by restoring the raw string with `ToHtmlString()` and rendering via `@Html.Raw` in the component view.
- **Grid styleship** — Umbraco ships the block-grid markup but no stylesheet, so I added the `.umb-block-grid` layout rules to the Frontend `site.css` (the local `Views/Partials/blockgrid/*` partials are untouched, per the rules).

## Anything not working / notes

- **Block Grid validation gotcha** — the Block Grid data type enforced its `validationLimit` literally (`max: 0` = zero blocks allowed) and every publish failed until I set the limits to `null`. Fixed via MCP before publishing.
- **Rich text double-encoding** — in v18 `IHtmlEncodedString` is *not* `IHtmlContent`, so `@Model.BodyText` emits escaped markup. Fixed by restoring the raw string with `ToHtmlString()` and rendering via `@Html.Raw` in the component view.
- **Grid styleship** — Umbraco ships the block-grid markup but no stylesheet, so I added the `.umb-block-grid` layout rules to the Frontend `site.css` (the local `Views/Partials/blockgrid/*` partials are untouched, per the rules).
- **Minor** — the front page's `intro` property currently serves as the page's meta description; the visible intro lives in the hero block. The pre-existing `SixLabors.ImageSharp` NuGet vulnerability warnings come from the scaffold's locked deps, not this work.
